newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly lower, but well off early lows linked to increased hog marketings and lower cash hog prices, traders said.
Pork bellies ended up in nearbys on strong cash belly values and lower in deferreds on projections USDA's Hogs and Pigs data Friday will show a larger hog herd, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.125 cent per lb higher to 0.925 lower with only October up and July off 0.150 at 82.250 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.000 cent higher to 1.000 lower with July up most at 82.100 cents.
Activity was kept light in both pits as traders awaited the release of USDA's quarterly report Friday, traders said.

Increased hogs marketings due to cooler weather in the Midwest weighed on hog futures early. But selling lacked active follow through and prices climbed back up to opening levels on scattered short covering, they said.

Analyst estimates on Friday's quarterly report put June 1 all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms at an average 102.9 percent of a year ago, in a range of 101.7 to 105 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 104.3 percent in a range of 103 to 106 percent and hogs kept for market averaged 102.6 percent of a year ago in a range of 101 to 105 percent.

Cargill Investor Services sold July along with spreaders who bought August. Local short covering supportive August along with buying from LFG and Rand Financials. Locals also bought October while E.D.&F. Man and Saul Stone sold, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission houses bought October 62 to 72 puts, December 66 to 70 puts, July 76 puts and July 84 calls. LFG activity bought August 76 puts, pit sources added.

Nearby pork belly futures again posted gains on a stronger tone to cash bellies. Cash bellies were again quoted higher, at $85 per cwt at noon, which reinforced gains, traders said. The price was the highest in three weeks, some sources said.
Next year contracts remained pressured by expectations the hog report will show increasing hog numbers and larger pork production next year, they added.
Locals covered short positions early to offset selling by ING and later buying by E.D.&F. Man and LFG took nearbys up to days highs, pit sources said.
